the school autonomy question is not about school autonomy as a universal concept.
the school autonomy question is not a question of ‘yes’ or ‘no’, but a question of ‘what kind of autonomy’ and ‘under which circumstances’.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are no universal solutions to the question of school autono­my.

there is no one-size-fits-all solution on the question of autonomy and that it is critical for school leadership policies to reflect on context-specific policies on autonomy that are adaptive and responsive to the divergent educational contexts and needs in European countries.

school leadership policy development should be seen as a continuous, context-sensitive process that is based on the active involvement and collaboration of school leaders, teachers, and school communities.

school autonomy should be seen as one of the key elements of school leadership policy, but not as a policy in itself.
school autonomy is a critical factor for the development of effective school leadership policies, but it is not an end in itself.
